Implementation: Batch Elasticsearch Comment Counts

Summary

Replaced per-comment Elasticsearch GET requests in ListComments and ListRepliesComment with one _mget request per page. Both endpoints now use the package-local getCommentCounts helper, which delegates transport work to the existing global ElasticSearch.RetrieveElasticBatch utility.

Changes

CommentCounts.go

Added:

  • getCommentCounts to create document IDs, call the global batch utility, decode each source, and map counters by comment slug.
  • decodeCommentCount to preserve the previous map representation and fallback values.

ListComments.go

  • Collects all comment slugs after the existing database query.
  • Retrieves all counter documents once.
  • Removes the Elasticsearch request from the response loop.
  • Assigns each existing ReplyComment value from the slug-keyed lookup.

ListRepliesComment.go

  • Collects reply slugs once.
  • Reuses the same slug slice for the existing liked-state batch query and the new counter batch query.
  • Removes the Elasticsearch request from the response loop.
  • Assigns each existing comment_count value from the slug-keyed lookup.

Data Flow

comment rows
  -> collect slugs
  -> build comment_<slug> document IDs
  -> one RetrieveElasticBatch call
  -> decode sources
  -> map counters by slug
  -> shape original response order

The Elasticsearch request is equivalent to:

POST /comment_<prefix>/_mget
Content-Type: application/json

{"ids":["comment_<slug-1>","comment_<slug-2>"]}

Counter Compatibility

Found source documents are decoded into map[string]interface{}, matching the previous V1RetrieveElastic result type. JSON numeric values therefore remain float64 during Go decoding, as before.

Missing or empty sources return:

{
  "counter_reply_comment": 0,
  "counter_like_comment": 0
}

A null or other non-object source returns an error, matching the previous source type validation.

Response Compatibility

  • ListComments still assigns counters to reply_comment.
  • ListRepliesComment still assigns counters to comment_count.
  • Counter field names and values remain unchanged.
  • Both loops still iterate the original database result, preserving order.
  • Viewer and authenticated-user responses retain identical counter behavior.
  • Reply liked-state uses the same existing boolean map.
  • Include filtering, encryption, pagination, and all other fields remain unchanged.

Query Impact

Before, per endpoint:

1 comment-list database query + N Elasticsearch GET requests

After:

1 comment-list database query + at most 1 Elasticsearch _mget request

ListRepliesComment also retains its single liked-state database query. The new counter batching does not add another slug collection loop.

Tests

CommentCounts_test.go verifies:

  • Existing counter values survive JSON decoding.
  • JSON numeric values use the same decoded type.
  • Missing sources receive the exact zero-counter fallback.
  • A null source returns an error instead of changing the response type.

The test was run before implementation and failed because decodeCommentCount did not exist. It passed after the minimal decoder and batch helper were added.

Verification

gofmt -l src/Action/V1/Comments/CommentCounts.go src/Action/V1/Comments/CommentCounts_test.go src/Action/V1/Comments/ListComments.go src/Action/V1/Comments/ListRepliesComment.go
go test -count=1 ./src/Action/V1/Comments
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • The focused Comments tests pass.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

ListComments and ListRepliesComment retrieved Elasticsearch counter documents separately for every returned comment. A page containing N comments or replies therefore executed N Elasticsearch requests only to populate the existing comment-count fields.

Both endpoints use the same index and document naming convention:

index: comment_<prefix>
document ID: comment_<slug>

Scope

  • Reuse the existing global ElasticSearch.RetrieveElasticBatch utility.
  • Add a package-local Comments helper for batch retrieval and counter decoding.
  • Retrieve all comment counter documents for a page with one _mget request.
  • Update ListComments.
  • Update ListRepliesComment.
  • Reuse the reply slug slice for both liked-state and counter batch queries.
  • Preserve missing and empty document fallback values.
  • Add focused tests for counter decoding, numeric types, fallback values, and invalid sources.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Comment and reply database queries, filters, ordering, and pagination.
  • reply_comment and comment_count response field names.
  • counter_reply_comment and counter_like_comment values and JSON types.
  • Zero-counter fallback for missing or empty Elasticsearch documents.
  • Reply liked-state behavior.
  • Comment text unescaping and short/long comment generation.
  • Include-field filtering.
  • Existing API error responses for Elasticsearch request or malformed source failures.
  • Encryption behavior and every mobile-facing response field.

Out of Scope

  • Changing Elasticsearch mappings or counter documents.
  • Batching post or folder counter indexes.
  • Changing comment or reply list queries.
  • Refactoring dedicated Slim, Worker, or Support files.
  • Changing response schemas, nesting, or field names.

Acceptance Criteria

  • ListComments performs at most one Elasticsearch counter request per page.
  • ListRepliesComment performs at most one Elasticsearch counter request per page.
  • Empty result pages perform no Elasticsearch request.
  • All comment_<slug> document IDs from the current page are included in the batch request.
  • Returned sources are assigned to the correct comment slugs.
  • Missing and empty sources produce both existing counters with value 0.
  • Invalid non-object sources retain existing error behavior.
  • Comment and reply ordering remains unchanged.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-07. No commit was created.

Implementation: Batch Folder Bookmark Enrichment

Summary

Replaced the three per-folder enrichment operations in ListFolderBookmarks and SearchFolderBookmark with three fixed batch operations per page. Shared behavior now lives in Utils/Functions/BookmarkFunctions because it is reused across the Bookmarks and Search packages.

Changes

FolderEnrichment.go

Added:

  • GetPOTDFolders to retrieve distinct broadcast folder IDs once and return a boolean lookup.
  • GetFolderBookmarkTotals to retrieve all folder_<slug> Elasticsearch documents through RetrieveElasticBatch.
  • GetFolderThumbnails to execute the shared top-four thumbnail query and group rows by folder ID.
  • folderThumbnailsQuery to apply per-folder ranking and the original filters.
  • groupFolderThumbnails to preserve row order and initialize empty slices.
  • folderBookmarkTotal to preserve raw Elasticsearch JSON and the existing missing-document fallback.

ListFolderBookmarks.go

  • Collects folder IDs once after loading the existing exclusion lists.
  • Loads POTD states, counters, and thumbnails before response shaping.
  • Removes all three per-folder enrichment requests from the response loop.
  • Preserves map-based standard and sl=true response construction.

SearchFolderBookmark.go

  • Uses the same batch helpers and folder ID list.
  • Removes all three per-folder enrichment requests from the response loop.
  • Preserves the existing Models.BookmarkFolder response.

Batch Thumbnail Query

The thumbnail query performs the equivalent of:

SELECT folder_id, thumbnail
FROM (
    SELECT
        folder_id,
        thumbnail,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY folder_id
            ORDER BY created_at DESC
        ) AS thumbnail_rank
    FROM views_list_bookmarks
    WHERE folder_id IN (:folder_ids)
      AND user_id = :user_id
      AND post_type != 'video360'
      AND slug NOT IN (:blocked_posts)
      AND encrypt NOT IN (:excluded_users)
) AS ranked_bookmarks
WHERE thumbnail_rank <= 4
ORDER BY folder_id, thumbnail_rank;

The two NOT IN clauses are only added when their corresponding exclusion lists are non-empty, matching the previous queries.

PARTITION BY folder_id is required because a global LIMIT 4 would return only four thumbnails across the complete page. Ranking restarts for each folder and therefore preserves the previous per-folder limit.

POTD and Counter Batches

POTD states use one query equivalent to:

SELECT DISTINCT folder_id
FROM broadcast
WHERE folder_id IN (:folder_ids);

Counter documents use one request equivalent to:

POST /folder_bookmarks_<prefix>/_mget
Content-Type: application/json

{"ids":["folder_<slug-1>","folder_<slug-2>"]}

Response Compatibility

  • Folder rows remain in the original database query order.
  • POTD and enrichment data are matched by folder ID instead of batch response position.
  • Thumbnail rows remain newest-first within each folder.
  • Folders without eligible thumbnails receive [], not null.
  • Found counter documents retain their original raw _source JSON.
  • Missing counter documents retain {"counter_bookmak":0} exactly.
  • ListFolderBookmarks still converts counter_bookmark to an integer only for sl=true.
  • Standard responses still return the original postgres.Jsonb counter representation.
  • Names, publication status, IDs, encryption, and every response field remain unchanged.

Request Impact

Before, per endpoint:

1 folder query + N POTD queries + N Elasticsearch requests + N thumbnail queries

After:

1 folder query + 1 POTD query + 1 Elasticsearch request + 1 thumbnail query

Tests

FolderEnrichment_test.go verifies:

  • Thumbnail rows remain in query order when grouped.
  • Folders without rows receive non-nil empty slices.
  • SQL ranks rows with PARTITION BY folder_id and created_at DESC.
  • SQL retains folder, user, post type, blocked-post, and excluded-user filters.
  • SQL applies thumbnail_rank <= 4 and orders by folder and rank.
  • Found counter JSON remains unchanged.
  • Missing counter documents retain the exact existing fallback.

The tests were run before implementation and failed because the new batch helpers did not exist. They passed after the minimal shared implementation was added.

Verification

gofmt -l src/Action/V1/Bookmarks/ListFolderBookmarks.go src/Action/V1/Search/SearchFolderBookmark.go src/Utils/Functions/BookmarkFunctions/FolderEnrichment.go src/Utils/Functions/BookmarkFunctions/FolderEnrichment_test.go
go test -count=1 ./src/Utils/Functions/BookmarkFunctions
go test -count=1 ./src/Action/V1/Bookmarks
go test -count=1 ./src/Action/V1/Search
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • Focused BookmarkFunctions, Bookmarks, and Search checks pass.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

ListFolderBookmarks and SearchFolderBookmark enriched every returned folder with three separate per-folder operations:

  1. A database query to determine POTD status.
  2. An Elasticsearch request for the bookmark counter.
  3. A database query for the four newest thumbnails.

A page containing N folders therefore executed 3N enrichment requests after the main folder query. Both endpoints used the same filters and returned the same enrichment data.

Scope

  • Add reusable folder bookmark helpers under Utils/Functions/BookmarkFunctions.
  • Retrieve POTD folder IDs with one database query.
  • Retrieve all folder bookmark counters with one Elasticsearch _mget request.
  • Retrieve the four newest thumbnails independently for every folder with one database query.
  • Group thumbnail rows by folder ID.
  • Update ListFolderBookmarks and SearchFolderBookmark to use the batch results.
  • Preserve all standard and sl=true response formats.
  • Add focused tests for per-folder thumbnail ranking, grouping, ordering, empty slices, and counter fallback.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Folder list and search queries, ordering, pagination, and ownership filters.
  • POTD boolean values.
  • Folder bookmark counter values and raw JSON representation.
  • The existing counter_bookmak fallback key for missing Elasticsearch documents.
  • A maximum of four newest thumbnails per folder.
  • Blocked-post, blocked-user, deactivated-user, and video360 thumbnail filters.
  • Empty thumbnail arrays for folders without eligible posts.
  • Standard and sl=true response fields, types, and nesting.
  • Existing database and Elasticsearch error responses.
  • Encryption behavior and mobile compatibility.

Out of Scope

  • Changing published-folder endpoints.
  • Changing folder search or pagination behavior.
  • Changing bookmark creation or deletion.
  • Correcting the existing counter_bookmak fallback spelling.
  • Adding new response fields.
  • Refactoring dedicated Slim, Worker, or Support files.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Each affected endpoint performs one POTD query per page instead of one per folder.
  • Each affected endpoint performs one Elasticsearch counter request per page instead of one per folder.
  • Each affected endpoint performs one thumbnail query per page instead of one per folder.
  • Empty folder pages execute no enrichment requests.
  • Thumbnail ranking restarts for every folder with PARTITION BY folder_id.
  • Each folder receives at most four thumbnails ordered by created_at DESC.
  • Folders without eligible posts receive a non-nil empty thumbnail slice.
  • Missing Elasticsearch documents retain the existing fallback JSON.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implementation: Batch Search Hashtag Posts

Summary

Replaced the per-hashtag post-preview query in SearchHashtag with one package-local batch query. PostgreSQL ROW_NUMBER() partitions rows by tag so each hashtag still receives at most four posts. Results are grouped by tag and assigned to the unchanged response model.

Changes

  • Added SearchHashtagPosts.go containing:
    • searchHashtagPostRow
    • getSearchHashtagPosts
    • searchHashtagPostsQuery
    • groupSearchHashtagPosts
  • Updated SearchHashtag.go to collect tags before response enrichment.
  • Replaced the query inside the hashtag loop with one batch lookup.
  • Added SearchHashtagPosts_test.go.
  • Added a code comment explaining why tag collection uses a separate loop.

Batch Query

The new query performs the equivalent of:

SELECT tag, slug, thumbnail
FROM (
    SELECT tag, slug, thumbnail,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tag) AS post_rank
    FROM views_hashtag
    WHERE tag IN (:tags)
) AS ranked_posts
WHERE post_rank <= 4
ORDER BY tag, post_rank;

post_rank is internal. It replaces the separate LIMIT 4 calls and is not returned by the API.

Why Per-Tag Ranking Is Required

A global LIMIT 4 would return four posts across all hashtags. PARTITION BY tag restarts ROW_NUMBER() for every tag, so post_rank <= 4 keeps up to four posts for each hashtag.

No ordering expression was added inside ROW_NUMBER(). The previous query had no ORDER BY, so adding one would introduce new response behavior.

Response Compatibility

  • The response still uses the existing Models.SearchHashtagPost type.
  • Only slug and thumbnail are assigned to each post preview.
  • Every requested tag is initialized with []Models.SearchHashtagPost{}.
  • Hashtags without rows therefore return posts: [], not null.
  • Hashtag result order remains controlled by the unchanged main query.
  • Batch query errors remain non-fatal and produce empty post slices.
  • No response field, type, encryption behavior, or mobile-facing schema changed.

Query Impact

Before:

1 hashtag search query + up to N post-preview queries

After:

1 hashtag search query + up to 1 post-preview query

Tests

Focused tests verify:

  • Rows are grouped under the correct tag.
  • Row order is retained during grouping.
  • Tags without posts receive a non-nil empty slice.
  • SQL uses ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tag).
  • SQL reads from views_hashtag and filters requested tags.
  • SQL limits each tag with post_rank <= 4.

Verification

gofmt -l src/Action/V1/Hashtag/SearchHashtag.go src/Action/V1/Hashtag/SearchHashtagPosts.go src/Action/V1/Hashtag/SearchHashtagPosts_test.go
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

SearchHashtag queried views_hashtag separately for every returned hashtag to retrieve up to four post previews. A result containing N hashtags therefore executed N additional post queries.

The refactor must reduce this repeated database work while preserving the existing response and the maximum of four posts for each hashtag.

Scope

  • Collect tags from the current hashtag search result.
  • Retrieve matching post previews with one batch query.
  • Rank rows independently for each tag.
  • Keep ranks 1 through 4 for every tag.
  • Group rows by tag.
  • Assign each grouped slice to the existing posts response field.
  • Add focused tests for query partitioning, per-tag limits, grouping, row order, and empty slices.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • The main hashtag search query, filters, ordering, limit, and offset.
  • A maximum of four post previews per hashtag.
  • Existing slug and thumbnail response fields.
  • posts: [] for hashtags without matching posts.
  • Existing non-fatal post-query error handling.
  • Existing unspecified post order because the previous query had no ORDER BY.
  • Every mobile-facing response field, type, and value rule.

Out of Scope

  • Changing hashtag search ranking or pagination.
  • Adding deterministic post ordering that did not exist before.
  • Adding post fields or returning the internal post_rank value.
  • Changing encryption behavior or response schemas.
  • Refactoring unrelated hashtag logic.

Acceptance Criteria

  • SearchHashtag performs at most one post-preview query for the current result page.
  • No post-preview query runs for an empty hashtag result.
  • The query ranks rows separately with PARTITION BY tag.
  • post_rank <= 4 preserves the old per-hashtag LIMIT 4 behavior.
  • Rows are grouped under the correct tags.
  • Hashtags without posts receive a non-nil empty slice.
  • Post-query failures still produce empty post slices without a new API error.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-08. No commit was created.

Implementation: Batch Broadcast Bookmark Enrichment

Summary

Moved the duplicated bookmark enrichment from ListBroadcast and ListPotdBroadcast into package-local helpers in BroadcastFunctions.go. Totals and latest previews are now loaded in two batch queries and grouped by folder ID before response construction.

Changes

  • Extended BroadcastFunctions.go with:
    • broadcastBookmarkCountRow
    • broadcastBookmarkPreviewRow
    • getBroadcastBookmarkData
    • broadcastBookmarkFolderIDs
    • broadcastBookmarkCountsQuery
    • broadcastBookmarkPreviewsQuery
    • groupBroadcastBookmarkData
  • Updated ListBroadcast.go to load bookmark enrichment once and reuse it by folder ID.
  • Updated ListPotdBroadcast.go to do the same only when bookmark is included.
  • Removed both duplicated per-row query blocks.
  • Extended BroadcastFunctions_test.go with focused bookmark enrichment tests.

Batch Queries

Bookmark totals are retrieved with one query equivalent to:

SELECT folder_id, total_bookmark
FROM views_total_bookmark_per_folder
WHERE folder_id IN (:folder_ids);

Latest bookmark previews are retrieved with one query equivalent to:

SELECT folder_id, thumbnail, name
FROM (
    SELECT b.folder_id, p.thumbnail, fb.name,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY b.folder_id
            ORDER BY b.created_at DESC
        ) AS bookmark_rank
    FROM bookmark b
    LEFT JOIN folder_bookmark fb ON fb.id = b.folder_id
    LEFT JOIN posts p ON p.id = b.post_id
    WHERE b.folder_id IN (:folder_ids)
) AS ranked_bookmarks
WHERE bookmark_rank = 1;

ROW_NUMBER() restarts for every folder. Selecting rank 1 therefore reproduces the previous per-folder ORDER BY b.created_at DESC LIMIT 1 behavior.

Response Compatibility

Every requested folder ID is initialized with:

map[string]interface{}{
    "total":     int64(0),
    "thumbnail": "",
    "name":      "",
}

Count and preview rows overwrite only their matching defaults. The resulting response therefore retains the previous field names, Go value types, and missing-row values.

ListPotdBroadcast calls the batch helper only when shouldInclude("bookmark") is true. Existing POTD field-selection behavior remains unchanged.

Query Impact

Before:

Up to 2 queries per bookmark broadcast
N bookmark broadcasts = up to 2N queries

After:

Up to 1 total query + 1 preview query per result page
N bookmark broadcasts = up to 2 queries

No query runs when the result contains no usable bookmark folder ID.

Test-Driven Verification

Focused tests were added before production code. The first run failed because the new folder collection, grouping, and query helpers were undefined.

After implementation, the tests verify:

  • Post broadcasts and empty folder IDs are excluded from bookmark enrichment.
  • Totals, thumbnails, and names are grouped under the correct folder ID.
  • Missing rows retain int64(0) and empty-string defaults.
  • The total query selects all requested folder IDs.
  • The preview query partitions by folder ID.
  • The preview query preserves newest-first selection and retains rank 1.

Scope Audit

  • 1 existing package-local helper file extended.
  • 2 related Broadcast endpoints updated.
  • 2 duplicated per-row query blocks removed.
  • No response model or mobile-facing schema changed.
  • No Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated code changed.
  • The existing API collection environment change was not modified.

Verification

gofmt -l src/Action/V1/Broadcast/BroadcastFunctions.go src/Action/V1/Broadcast/BroadcastFunctions_test.go src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListBroadcast.go src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListPotdBroadcast.go
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

ListBroadcast and ListPotdBroadcast contained the same bookmark enrichment block. For every bookmark broadcast, each endpoint queried the bookmark total and latest bookmark preview separately. A page containing N bookmark broadcasts therefore executed up to 2N additional queries.

The refactor must centralize this sibling logic and batch the database work without changing either response.

Scope

  • Collect non-empty folder IDs from bookmark broadcasts.
  • Retrieve bookmark totals for all folder IDs with one query.
  • Retrieve the latest bookmark thumbnail and folder name for all folder IDs with one query.
  • Rank bookmark rows independently for each folder by created_at DESC.
  • Group totals and previews by folder ID.
  • Reuse the package-local enrichment from ListBroadcast and ListPotdBroadcast.
  • Preserve the POTD include=bookmark condition.
  • Add focused tests for folder filtering, response mapping, defaults, and query rules.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Existing Broadcast and POTD main queries, filters, ordering, limits, and offsets.
  • The latest bookmark selection for each folder.
  • Bookmark response fields total, thumbnail, and name.
  • total as int64.
  • Empty-string defaults for thumbnail and name when no bookmark preview exists.
  • A zero total when no total row exists.
  • Existing POTD include behavior.
  • Existing internal-server-error responses when enrichment queries fail.
  • Every mobile-facing response field and type.

Out of Scope

  • Changing post broadcast enrichment.
  • Changing Broadcast or POTD response schemas.
  • Changing bookmark filtering or folder visibility rules.
  • Updating Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated endpoints.
  • Combining both batch queries into a more complex database query.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Both Broadcast list endpoints use one package-local bookmark enrichment path.
  • No per-broadcast bookmark total or preview query remains in either response loop.
  • A result page executes at most one total query and one preview query.
  • No enrichment query runs when the result contains no bookmark folder IDs.
  • The preview query uses PARTITION BY b.folder_id and ORDER BY b.created_at DESC.
  • Only bookmark_rank = 1 is retained for each folder.
  • Missing total and preview rows retain the previous response defaults.
  • POTD skips bookmark enrichment when bookmark is excluded.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-08. No commit was created.

issues.display_title: Issue #546: Batch Search Published Folder POTD Status
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Batch Search Published Folder POTD Status

Summary

Replaced the per-folder POTD query in SearchPublishedFolderBookmark with the existing global BookmarkFunctions.GetPOTDFolders batch helper. Folder IDs are collected once, queried once, and matched back to search results by UUID.

Changes

SearchPublishedFolderBookmark.go

  • Added BookmarkFunctions and UUID imports.
  • Collected valid folder UUIDs before response construction.
  • Called BookmarkFunctions.GetPOTDFolders once for the complete result page.
  • Replaced the per-folder broadcast query with a map lookup.
  • Preserved ignored POTD query errors so lookup failure still produces false.
  • Added a comment explaining the two-loop structure.

FolderEnrichment.go

  • Extracted the existing query construction into potdFoldersQuery.
  • Kept GetPOTDFolders behavior and public signature unchanged.
  • Continued using SELECT DISTINCT folder_id and one folder_id IN filter.

FolderEnrichment_test.go

  • Added focused coverage for the shared POTD batch query.
  • Verified distinct folder selection, the broadcast table, and the batch IN condition.

Query Flow

Before:

Load N folders
For each folder:
    SELECT id FROM broadcast WHERE folder_id = :folder_id

After:

Load N folders
Collect folder IDs
SELECT DISTINCT folder_id
FROM broadcast
WHERE folder_id IN (:folder_ids)
Map each result by folder ID

The database work changes from N POTD queries to at most one POTD query.

Response Compatibility

The old code set Potd to true only when its individual query succeeded and returned at least one row. All other cases produced false.

The batch helper returns a map containing only folder IDs found in broadcast:

folderBookmark[i].Potd = potdFolders[folderID]

Go map lookup returns false for a missing key. This preserves the previous results:

  • Folder found in broadcast: potd: true.
  • Folder not found: potd: false.
  • Invalid folder UUID: potd: false.
  • Batch query error: the returned nil map is read as false for every folder.

The endpoint continues ignoring POTD lookup errors instead of returning a new API error. Main search results, ordering, includes, encryption, and all response fields remain unchanged.

Why Two Loops Remain

The first loop collects folder IDs required by the batch query. The second loop preserves the existing response shaping for names, users, totals, and POTD flags.

This avoids a database query inside the response loop while retaining linear in-memory work.

Test-Driven Verification

The query test was added before production changes. Its first run failed because potdFoldersQuery did not exist.

After implementation, focused tests verify that the shared helper builds one distinct batch query for all folder IDs. Existing BookmarkFunctions and Search tests also pass.

Scope Audit

  • 1 published-folder search endpoint updated.
  • 1 existing global helper reused.
  • 1 package-private query builder extracted for verification.
  • 1 per-folder database query removed.
  • No response model or mobile-facing schema changed.
  • No detail, Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated endpoint changed.
  • The existing API collection environment change was not modified.

Verification

gofmt -l src/Action/V1/Search/SearchPublishedFolderBookmark.go src/Utils/Functions/BookmarkFunctions/FolderEnrichment.go src/Utils/Functions/BookmarkFunctions/FolderEnrichment_test.go
go test -count=1 ./src/Utils/Functions/BookmarkFunctions ./src/Action/V1/Search
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • Focused BookmarkFunctions and Search tests pass.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

SearchPublishedFolderBookmark queried the broadcast table separately for every published folder to determine its POTD status. A result page containing N folders therefore executed N additional database queries.

The repository already provides BookmarkFunctions.GetPOTDFolders for the same batch lookup. The search endpoint must reuse it without changing its response or query-error behavior.

Scope

  • Collect folder IDs from the current published-folder search result.
  • Convert the model's string folder IDs to UUID values for the existing shared helper.
  • Retrieve all matching POTD folder IDs through BookmarkFunctions.GetPOTDFolders.
  • Assign each folder's existing Potd field from the returned lookup map.
  • Keep a comment explaining why ID collection and response construction use separate loops.
  • Add focused coverage for the shared batch query shape.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • The main published-folder query, filters, ordering, limit, and offset.
  • Existing name escaping, user mapping, and bookmark-total formatting.
  • The potd response field and boolean type.

issues.display_title: Issue #547: Batch Check Status Upload Multiple Posts
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Batch Check Status Upload Multiple Posts

Summary

Replaced the per-uploading-post multiple_post query in CheckStatusPostUpload with one package-local batch query. Query rows are grouped by post ID and passed through the existing Redis reconciliation and per-post update flow.

Changes

CheckStatusPostUpload.go

  • Collects uploading post IDs before reconciliation.
  • Executes one multiple_post query for all collected IDs.
  • Selects both post_id and path so rows can be grouped correctly.
  • Uses groupMultiplePostPaths to create a post-ID lookup.
  • Reuses each post's grouped rows in the existing loop.
  • Keeps Redis cleanup and is_uploading updates per post.
  • Adds a comment explaining why ID collection requires a separate loop.

Added package-local helpers:

  • multiplePostPathsQuery
  • groupMultiplePostPaths

CheckStatusPostUpload_test.go

  • Verifies rows are grouped under the correct post IDs in query order.
  • Verifies non-string path values remain in the grouped rows.
  • Verifies the query selects post_id and path from multiple_post.
  • Verifies the query uses one post_id IN condition.

Query Flow

Before:

Load N uploading posts
For each post:
    SELECT path FROM multiple_post WHERE post_id = :post_id
    Reconcile Redis keys
    Update is_uploading

After:

Load N uploading posts
Collect post IDs
SELECT post_id, path
FROM multiple_post
WHERE post_id IN (:post_ids)
Group rows by post ID
For each post:
    Reconcile Redis keys
    Update is_uploading

The repeated database read changes from N queries to at most one query. Redis work and post updates remain per post.

Flow Compatibility

For each successfully loaded post group, the existing flow remains:

  1. If no multiple_post rows exist, delete all panorama-status keys for the post.
  2. Otherwise, retrieve the post's Redis keys.
  3. When counts differ, derive filenames from the stored paths.
  4. Delete Redis keys without matching multiple_post filenames.
  5. Update that post's is_uploading value to false.

The grouped data retains complete row maps instead of only normalized path strings. This preserves the old row count and the existing path string type check, including rows containing null or non-string path values.

Error Compatibility

The previous per-post query used continue when the query failed. The batch query error is also retained as a non-fatal condition. When it fails, each uploading post is skipped, no Redis cleanup or status update runs, and the endpoint returns its existing successful response.

Redis lookup errors still skip only the affected post. Database status updates remain separate and retain their existing ignored-error behavior.

Response Compatibility

The response remains:

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "total_uploading": 0,
    "message": "Status check completed"
  }
}

total_uploading still uses the original uploading-post result length. No response field, type, value rule, or status code changed.

Test-Driven Verification

Tests were added before production code. The first test run failed because groupMultiplePostPaths and multiplePostPathsQuery were undefined.

After implementation, focused tests confirm grouping and query behavior. The complete repository checks also pass.

Scope Audit

  • 1 existing Posts action file updated.
  • 1 focused test file added.
  • 1 per-post database read removed.
  • Redis cleanup remains per post.
  • Database status updates remain per post.
  • No response model or mobile-facing schema changed.
  • No Worker, Slim, Support, or unrelated code changed.
  • The existing API collection environment change was not modified.

Verification

gofmt -l src/Action/V1/Posts/CheckStatusPostUpload.go src/Action/V1/Posts/CheckStatusPostUpload_test.go
go test -count=1 ./src/Action/V1/Posts
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • Both changed Go files are formatted.
  • Focused Posts tests pass.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

CheckStatusPostUpload queried multiple_post separately for every uploading post before reconciling its Redis panorama-status keys. A request containing N uploading posts therefore executed N additional read queries.

The refactor must batch only this repeated read while preserving the endpoint's Redis cleanup, per-post status update, failure handling, and response.

Scope

  • Collect IDs from the current uploading-post result.
  • Retrieve post_id and path for all posts with one multiple_post query.
  • Group the returned rows by post ID.
  • Reuse the grouped rows during the existing per-post reconciliation loop.
  • Keep Redis cleanup operations per post.
  • Keep is_uploading updates per successfully processed post.
  • Add focused tests for grouping and batch query construction.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • The uploading-post query and its user, publication, and upload-status filters.
  • The returned total_uploading count.
  • Deletion of all panorama-status keys when a post has no multiple_post rows.
  • Comparison between Redis key count and multiple_post row count.
  • Existing path-to-filename extraction.
  • Deletion of orphaned Redis panorama-status keys.
  • Skipping a post when its multiple-post lookup fails.
  • Skipping a post when its Redis lookup fails.
  • Per-post is_uploading = false updates after successful processing.
  • Every response field, type, status code, and message.

Out of Scope

  • Batching Redis operations, because keys are scoped by post slug.
  • Batching is_uploading updates, which would change per-post failure isolation and update timing.
  • Changing filename parsing or panorama-status key formats.
  • Changing upload completion rules.
  • Updating Worker, Slim, Support, or unrelated endpoints.

Acceptance Criteria

  • At most one multiple_post read query runs per request.
  • No multiple_post query runs when there are no uploading posts.
  • The batch query selects post_id and path with one post_id IN filter.
  • Rows remain grouped under the correct post ID.
  • Row order and non-string path values remain available to the existing reconciliation logic.
  • A batch query failure skips all post processing while preserving the successful API response.
  • Redis cleanup and database updates remain inside the per-post flow.
  • The response schema remains unchanged.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-08. No commit was created.

Implementation: Batch Broadcast Bookmark Enrichment

Summary

Moved the duplicated bookmark enrichment from ListBroadcast and ListPotdBroadcast into package-local helpers in BroadcastFunctions.go. Totals and latest previews are now loaded in two batch queries and grouped by folder ID before response construction.

Changes

  • Extended BroadcastFunctions.go with:
    • broadcastBookmarkCountRow
    • broadcastBookmarkPreviewRow
    • getBroadcastBookmarkData
    • broadcastBookmarkFolderIDs
    • broadcastBookmarkCountsQuery
    • broadcastBookmarkPreviewsQuery
    • groupBroadcastBookmarkData
  • Updated ListBroadcast.go to load bookmark enrichment once and reuse it by folder ID.
  • Updated ListPotdBroadcast.go to do the same only when bookmark is included.
  • Removed both duplicated per-row query blocks.
  • Extended BroadcastFunctions_test.go with focused bookmark enrichment tests.

Batch Queries

Bookmark totals are retrieved with one query equivalent to:

SELECT folder_id, total_bookmark
FROM views_total_bookmark_per_folder
WHERE folder_id IN (:folder_ids);

Latest bookmark previews are retrieved with one query equivalent to:

SELECT folder_id, thumbnail, name
FROM (
    SELECT b.folder_id, p.thumbnail, fb.name,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY b.folder_id
            ORDER BY b.created_at DESC
        ) AS bookmark_rank
    FROM bookmark b
    LEFT JOIN folder_bookmark fb ON fb.id = b.folder_id
    LEFT JOIN posts p ON p.id = b.post_id
    WHERE b.folder_id IN (:folder_ids)
) AS ranked_bookmarks
WHERE bookmark_rank = 1;

ROW_NUMBER() restarts for every folder. Selecting rank 1 therefore reproduces the previous per-folder ORDER BY b.created_at DESC LIMIT 1 behavior.

Response Compatibility

Every requested folder ID is initialized with:

map[string]interface{}{
    "total":     int64(0),
    "thumbnail": "",
    "name":      "",
}

Count and preview rows overwrite only their matching defaults. The resulting response therefore retains the previous field names, Go value types, and missing-row values.

ListPotdBroadcast calls the batch helper only when shouldInclude("bookmark") is true. Existing POTD field-selection behavior remains unchanged.

Query Impact

Before:

Up to 2 queries per bookmark broadcast
N bookmark broadcasts = up to 2N queries

After:

Up to 1 total query + 1 preview query per result page
N bookmark broadcasts = up to 2 queries

No query runs when the result contains no usable bookmark folder ID.

Test-Driven Verification

Focused tests were added before production code. The first run failed because the new folder collection, grouping, and query helpers were undefined.

After implementation, the tests verify:

  • Post broadcasts and empty folder IDs are excluded from bookmark enrichment.
  • Totals, thumbnails, and names are grouped under the correct folder ID.
  • Missing rows retain int64(0) and empty-string defaults.
  • The total query selects all requested folder IDs.
  • The preview query partitions by folder ID.
  • The preview query preserves newest-first selection and retains rank 1.

Scope Audit

  • 1 existing package-local helper file extended.
  • 2 related Broadcast endpoints updated.
  • 2 duplicated per-row query blocks removed.
  • No response model or mobile-facing schema changed.
  • No Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated code changed.
  • The existing API collection environment change was not modified.

Verification

gofmt -l src/Action/V1/Broadcast/BroadcastFunctions.go src/Action/V1/Broadcast/BroadcastFunctions_test.go src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListBroadcast.go src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListPotdBroadcast.go
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

ListBroadcastBookmark first loaded all eligible bookmark post IDs, then queried the post and user details separately for every ID. A folder containing N eligible posts therefore executed one ID query followed by N detail queries.

The refactor must replace only the repeated detail lookup while preserving the original ID filtering, result order, response models, and failure behavior.

Scope

  • Keep the existing bookmark post-ID query and exclusion filters.
  • Retrieve all post and user details with one batch query.
  • Include post ID only as an internal grouping key.
  • Map query rows by post ID.
  • Rebuild the response slice following the original post-ID order.
  • Preserve nested user construction.
  • Add focused tests for query shape, ordering, and nested user data.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Broadcast lookup by slug.
  • Existing blocked-post, blocked-user, and deactivated-user filtering.
  • The order returned by the original bookmark post-ID query.
  • Every BroadcastBookmark field and pointer type.
  • Existing nested user fields and values.
  • A non-nil empty bookmarks slice when no eligible post ID exists.
  • The existing internal-server-error response when a post-detail query fails.
  • The existing ignored error behavior of the initial post-ID query.
  • Encryption and every mobile-facing response field and type.

Out of Scope

  • Combining the initial ID query with the detail query.
  • Adding new ordering to the bookmark ID query.
  • Changing bookmark visibility or exclusion rules.
  • Changing Broadcast response models.
  • Updating Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated endpoints.

Acceptance Criteria

  • At most one post-and-user detail query runs for all eligible post IDs.
  • No detail query runs when the post-ID result is empty.
  • The batch query selects all fields previously loaded per post.
  • The batch query filters with one p.id IN condition.
  • Results are matched by post ID and emitted in original post-ID order.
  • Nested user data remains populated from avatar, fullname, and username.
  • The internal post ID does not appear in the API response.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

issues.display_title: Issue #549: Centralize Place Detail Request Setup
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Place Detail Request Setup

Summary

Added preparePlaceDetailRequest as a package-local helper and replaced the duplicated setup in four Place Detail endpoints. The helper returns authorization state, the user exclusion list, and the encryption timestamp without writing an HTTP response.

Changes

PlaceDetailRequest.go

Added:

  • placeDetailRequest
  • preparePlaceDetailRequest

The result contains:

  • notInEncrypt for deactivated and blocked-user filtering.
  • lastLogin for response encryption metadata.
  • unauthorized so each handler retains ownership of its existing HTTP 401 response.

Updated handlers

  • PlaceDetailHeader.go
  • PlaceDetailBookmarks.go
  • PlaceDetailContributors.go
  • PlaceDetailPosts.go

Each handler now consumes the shared setup through:

request := preparePlaceDetailRequest(c, role, encrypt)
if request.unauthorized {
	return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 401, fiber.ErrUnauthorized.Message, "Unauthorized")
}
notInEncrypt := request.notInEncrypt
currentLastLogin := request.lastLogin

Unused context, time, Redis, and user-function imports were removed from the four handlers.

PlaceDetailRequest_test.go

Added a focused test proving an unsupported role is marked unauthorized before Fiber, Redis, or user-data dependencies are accessed.

Shared Flow

preparePlaceDetailRequest performs the original matching operations in the same order:

  1. Reject roles other than user and viewer.
  2. Load deactivated users with Redis.GetEncodedStringList.
  3. Set the default current timestamp using the original format.
  4. For a user, retrieve data through UserFunctions.UserDatas.
  5. Report unauthorized state when user data is invalid.
  6. Replace the timestamp with last_login.
  7. Load the authenticated user's blocked users.
  8. Append blocked users after deactivated users.

Validation Order Compatibility

The helper call remains at the location of each original shared block:

  • Header still validates required location_group_slug first.
  • Posts still validates sort, normalizes search, calculates pagination, and validates nearest coordinates first.
  • Bookmarks and Contributors still calculate pagination first.

No endpoint-specific validation moved into the helper.

Response and Query Compatibility

  • Each handler still creates the same HTTP 401 response itself.
  • Redis key names and decoding behavior are unchanged.
  • GetEncodedStringList remains in use, so a missing or invalid Redis value still produces an empty list without invoking a database fallback.
  • Deactivated and blocked-user exclusion order is unchanged.
  • Viewer requests still use only deactivated-user exclusions and the generated timestamp.
  • User requests still use both exclusion sources and the stored last_login.
  • SQL tables, selects, joins, filters, ordering, limits, offsets, and scans are unchanged.
  • Response messages, keys, values, types, encryption inputs, and viewer e4 behavior are unchanged.

Test-Driven Verification

The focused test was added before production code. Its first run failed with:

undefined: preparePlaceDetailRequest

After implementation, the focused package test and complete repository checks passed.

Scope Audit

  • 1 package-local helper file added.
  • 1 focused test file added.
  • 4 related Place Detail handlers updated.
  • No endpoint-specific query or response code moved.
  • No global utility or new dependency added.
  • No Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated endpoint changed.
  • The existing API collection environment edit was not modified.

Verification

gofmt -w src/Action/V1/Places/PlaceDetailRequest.go src/Action/V1/Places/PlaceDetailRequest_test.go src/Action/V1/Places/PlaceDetailHeader.go src/Action/V1/Places/PlaceDetailBookmarks.go src/Action/V1/Places/PlaceDetailContributors.go src/Action/V1/Places/PlaceDetailPosts.go
go test -count=1 ./src/Action/V1/Places
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • Focused Places tests pass.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

Four related Place Detail endpoints repeated the same request preparation flow:

  • PlaceDetailHeader.go
  • PlaceDetailBookmarks.go
  • PlaceDetailContributors.go
  • PlaceDetailPosts.go

Each endpoint validated the caller role, loaded deactivated users, resolved the response encryption timestamp, validated authenticated user data, loaded blocked users, and combined the exclusion list. Maintaining the same flow in four files could cause authorization or visibility filtering to drift.

Scope

  • Add one package-local request preparation helper in the Places package.
  • Centralize the matching role validation state, last-login resolution, and Redis exclusion-list loading.
  • Update all four Place Detail endpoints to consume the prepared request data.
  • Keep endpoint-specific parameter validation, pagination, database queries, response construction, and encryption logic in their existing handlers.
  • Add one focused test for rejecting unsupported roles before request dependencies are accessed.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Accepted roles: user and viewer only.
  • The existing HTTP 401 response for unsupported roles and invalid user data.
  • Deactivated-user Redis key <prefix>_deactive_users_ec.
  • Blocked-user Redis key <prefix>_blocked_users_ec_<encrypt>.
  • Deactivated users before blocked users in notInEncrypt.
  • The default timestamp format 2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000.
  • Retrieval of authenticated user data through UserFunctions.UserDatas.
  • Use of the authenticated user's last_login value.
  • Viewer behavior without a blocked-user lookup.
  • Existing validation order in every endpoint.
  • Existing database queries, filters, ordering, pagination, and error responses.
  • Existing encrypted and unencrypted response structures, fields, types, and values.

Out of Scope

  • Moving the helper to a global utility because its current contract is specific to the four Place Detail handlers.
  • Updating GetPlaceList, GetPlaceSuggest, or PlaceDetailPostsSuggest, whose setup flows are not identical.
  • Replacing GetEncodedStringList with GetDeactiveUser, because the latter has different Redis-miss behavior.
  • Changing Redis fallback behavior or visibility rules.
  • Changing any mobile-facing API contract.
  • Refactoring Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated endpoints.

Acceptance Criteria

  • One package-local helper owns the duplicated Place Detail request setup.
  • All four scoped handlers use the helper.
  • Duplicated role, user-data, timestamp, and user-exclusion setup is removed from the callers.
  • Endpoint-specific validation still runs at the same point as before.
  • Invalid roles are rejected before Redis or user-data dependencies are accessed.
  • No query or response behavior changes.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-08. No commit was created.
